newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND LEAD BY 80 AT END OF SECOND DAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND LEAD BY 80 AT END OF SECOND DAY.

text.p: England led by 80 runs with seven first innings wickets standing to put them in command at the end of the second day of the second test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve on Friday.
Led by a fired-up Darren Gough, England scuttled New Zealand for 124 in the morning and then batted steadily on a tricky but flattening wicket to reach 204 for three wickets.

The wicket offered lift and movement for the seamers and slow turn for the spinners but England had solid contributions from in-form batsman Alec Stewart, captain Mike Atherton, Nasser Hussain and Graham Thorpe.
Hussain who reached his half century in 140 minutes was not out on 60 and Thorpe was on 47 in an unbroken stand of 98.

Hussain mixed aggression with caution. He smashed Dipak Patel for a six and four in the offspinner's first over but then retreated into his shell for long periods allowing debutant teenage left-armer Daniel Vettori to dominate him.

Stewart made a cultured 52 and looked on his way to his third test century in as many tests when he was brilliantly caught by a diving Stephen Fleming at first slip off left-armer Geoff Allott for 52.
After losing Nick Knight with the score on 10 before lunch, Stewart and Atherton set purposefully about overhauling New Zealand's modest score.
The pair put on 70 in just over even time and despite the bowlers still being able to extract considerable movement and lift, were able to drive with freedom at times.
Atherton looked well set on 30, having just imperiously off- driven Simon Doull to the boundary when the seam bowler had him trapped leg before playing forward.
Stewart, who scored 101 not out in the second test against Zimbabwe and 173 in the drawn first test in Auckland, reached his 50 in 76 balls and hit six boundaries.
Both the young left-armers, Allott with his quicks and Vettori with his slows, troubled the batsmen but with scant reward.
In the morning New Zealand, resuming at 56 for six, offered some resistance through Nathan Astle (36) and Patel (45), but Gough, Andrew Caddick and Dominic Cork completed the rout.
The aggressive Gough ended with five for 40 off 16 overs, his second five-wicket test bag.
New Zealand-raised Caddick, in a return to test cricket, did the Kiwis no favours, finishing with four for 45.
